turns.text: Hey there, how have things been?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can you explain ser and estar in Spanish? I keep getting them wrong.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sure. Both mean to be. Ser is for what something is, its identity or nature. Estar is for states and locations, how or where something is right now.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: So I'm tired would be estar?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Exactly, estoy cansado. It's a state that will change. But I'm tall is soy alto, because it's part of who you are.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Estoy en casa. Location is almost always estar.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Okay but then, why is it

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good catch. Where you're from is part of your identity, so it's ser. Your origin doesn't change.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Huh. That actually makes sense now.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Practise a few sentences about yourself, and it'll start feeling natural.
